decision: root cause of the lost frame length: the driver opens one register group per control write, and on this sensor a launched group lands two frame boundaries later and is discarded when another group opens first
why: raw register sequences on the live sensor: VTS group then exposure group loses VTS even 40 ms apart, one group or no group keeps it, and exposure changed every frame through the driver never reaches the sensor

decision: fork: write VTS, exposure and gain directly as one burst per register with no register group, not one group per control
why: direct writes land one frame later at any phase and never cancel each other, bursts keep each multi-byte register whole, and the Windows driver writes these registers the same way. A group per control only works with 0x3802 cleared and every group carrying the full state
evidence: /tmp/camre/work-driver/x2.txt (raw alternation lands every frame), x3.txt (bursts, gain lag), x4.txt (0x3802=0), sc200pc_decomp.c:6419-6518
result: chosen, HAL lag settings must drop from 2 to 1 frame
